$\text{E}[X]=$

activity_context.topic_title: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables

feedback.problem:
A production analyst records the number of flawed units in sampled batches. The data are summarized below. If $X$ is the number of flawed units in a batch, what is the expected value of $X?$

| Number of Batches | $10$ | $9$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flawed Units | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |

$\text{E}[X]=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

We're given the frequencies of the flawed units, so we can start by computing the corresponding probabilities. The total number of batches is $10+9+6=25,$ so the corresponding probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0)=f(0) & =\frac{10}{25} \\ P(X=1)=f(1) & =\frac{9}{25} \\ P(X=2)=f(2) & =\frac{6}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

We organize these results in the table below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{10}{25}$ | $\frac{9}{25}$ | $\frac{6}{25}$ |

Now, summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{10}{25})+1(\frac{9}{25})+2(\frac{6}{25}) \\  & =\frac{9}{25}+\frac{12}{25} \\  & =\frac{21}{25} \\  & =0.84.\end{aligned}
$$
